instructions: NextShell lends you the terminal tabs the user already opened; you never see credentials. session_list shows open tabs; host_list finds saved hosts and session_open opens one. exec runs a command on the remote host of a connected tab; session_send_text types into the tab itself and session_read (with waitFor/sinceCursor) reads what came back. Every change needs the user's approval in NextShell unless they enabled auto-approve for a while; on { status: 'pending', requestId } call the same tool again with the same arguments (or only the requestId). Risky commands (privilege escalation, recursive deletes, piping into a shell, package or service changes, writes to system directories) are ALWAYS a manual approval, even under auto-approve; `denied` means stop and ask the user; `forbidden` is final; `consent_required` means a credential file or the environment is involved: ask the user first. session_open answers { status: 'user_action_required' } while the user must answer a host-key, password or one-time-code dialog in the app: tell the user and call session_open again later. After the first action NextShell does not raise windows or switch tabs for you; session_focus is the explicit hand-over to the user. Outputs are redacted. agent_status shows your pending requests.

tools.description: Find saved servers by substring of name, host or tags (case-insensitive; matched against the redacted text). Returns metadata only, never credentials, plus `total` matches; page with `limit` (1-200, default 50) and `offset`. Use a host id as session_open's target.

query.description: Substring to look for; empty lists everything.

tools.name: host_list
tools.title: 查找服务器

tools.description: List the terminal tabs open in NextShell: session id, title, cwd, whether it is a local shell, and whether it is still connected. Pass a connected session id as target to the other tools. A session that is no longer connected answers `disconnected` there.
tools.name: session_list
tools.title: 列出会话

tools.description: Read a live session. Without options it returns the visible screen (secrets redacted; `lines` counts back from the bottom, default 200, max 2000) and a `cursor`. With `sinceCursor` it returns only the output received after that cursor (escape sequences removed, redacted), so you can follow a command typed with session_send_text. With `waitFor` it blocks until the text appears in that new output (or timeoutSec passes, max 60), then returns `matched` and `timedOut`; without sinceCursor it waits for output arriving from now on. The pattern is matched against the redacted text. Local shell tabs have no output stream: waitFor polls the screen and sinceCursor is unavailable.

lines.description: Lines counted back from the bottom (default 200).

mode.description: Only `screen` exists; incremental reads are selected by sinceCursor/waitFor.

sinceCursor.description: Opaque cursor from an earlier session_read or session_send_text response; return what arrived after it.

target.description: Live session id returned by session_list (or session_open).

waitFor.description: Wait until this appears in the new output.

pattern.description: A substring, or a Go (RE2) regular expression when it starts with `re:` (^ and $ match at line boundaries). Max 200 characters.

tools.name: session_read
tools.title: 读取会话屏幕

tools.description: Per-command history of a session. Currently reports integrationAvailable:false with no entries (it needs OSC 133 prompt marks); use session_read instead.

target.description: Live session id returned by session_list (or session_open).

tools.name: session_history
tools.title: 读取会话命令记录

tools.description: Search the user's saved command library by substring of name or command (matched against the redacted text), so you can reuse commands the user curated. Returns `total`; page with `limit` (1-200, default 50) and `offset`.

query.description: Substring to look for; empty lists everything.

tools.name: command_search
tools.title: 检索命令库

tools.description: Open a connection to a saved host (id from host_list) and return the new session id. A host that already has a connected tab is reused. The tab opens in the background: it does not switch tabs or take the keyboard. Needs the user's approval in NextShell unless they turned on auto-approve: the first call may return { status: 'pending', requestId }; call again with the same arguments. A `denied` error means the user refused: stop and ask them, never retry on your own. If the connection needs a decision from the user (trust a host key, type a password or one-time code) the call returns at once with { status: 'user_action_required', reason: 'host_key'|'host_key_changed'|'password'|'otp' } while the dialog stays open in the app (host_key_changed: the server's key differs from the trusted one; password with savedPasswordRejected: true: the saved password was rejected): tell the user, then call session_open again with the same target; it joins the pending connection. Failures say why: host_key, auth_failed, refused, unreachable, timeout.

reason.description: Shown to the user in the approval prompt.

requestId.description: Optional shortcut to continue an earlier { status: 'pending' } request (it lives 2 minutes): pass the requestId instead of repeating the arguments. Repeating the identical call also continues it.

tools.name: session_open
tools.title: 请求打开服务器

tools.description: Save a command in the user's library, or update one: pass an `id` from command_search and only the fields you want to change (the others are kept). An unknown id or workspaceId answers `not_found`. Without an id, name and command are required. Needs approval like exec.

appendCr.description: Press Enter after inserting the command.

command.description: The command text (required for a new command).

group.description: Group name; an empty string clears it.

id.description: Command id from command_search; update that command, merging only the fields provided.

name.description: Display name (required for a new command).

reason.description: Shown to the user in the approval prompt.

requestId.description: Optional shortcut to continue an earlier { status: 'pending' } request (it lives 2 minutes): pass the requestId instead of repeating the arguments. Repeating the identical call also continues it.

workspaceId.description: Cloud workspace to save into (new commands only); omit for the local library.

tools.name: command_save
tools.title: 保存快速命令

tools.description: Run a shell command on the REMOTE host of a connected session over a separate channel (invisible in the tab; local shell tabs are not supported). Returns output, stderr, exitCode and actualCwd, with secrets redacted; one exec at a time per session (`busy` otherwise). Needs the user's approval in NextShell unless they turned on auto-approve: the first call may return { status: 'pending', requestId } while the prompt is up; call exec again with the same arguments. `denied` means the user refused: stop and ask them, never retry on your own. Three tiers: forbidden commands (wiping disks or /, power off, kill everything, overwriting /etc/passwd, your user's blacklist) fail with `forbidden` and never run; risky commands (sudo/su, rm -r, piping into a shell or interpreter, eval, writes to /etc /boot /usr /var/lib, package or service changes, firewall, userdel/passwd) are ALWAYS a manual approval even under auto-approve (status `pending`, with `tier` and `why`); commands touching credential files (.env*, ssh keys, .aws/credentials, .netrc, …) or dumping the environment (env, printenv, set) fail with `consent_required` until the user agrees; then pass allowSensitive: true (also a manual approval). `timeoutSec` max 120 (default 30).

allowSensitive.description: Set only after the user agreed that credential files or the environment may be touched.

command.description: Shell command to run on the remote host.

mode.description: Only `background` exists: a separate channel, invisible in the tab. Interactive input goes through session_send_text.

reason.description: Shown to the user in the approval prompt.

requestId.description: Optional shortcut to continue an earlier { status: 'pending' } request (it lives 2 minutes): pass the requestId instead of repeating the arguments. Repeating the identical call also continues it.

target.description: Live session id returned by session_list (or session_open).

timeoutSec.description: Seconds before the command is cancelled, 1-120 (default 30).

tools.name: exec
tools.title: 在会话里执行命令

tools.description: Type into the terminal tab itself, like a user would: `text` (up to 4 KiB; the escapes \r \n \t \e \xHH and \\ are interpreted, so use \\ for a literal backslash) and/or named `keys` (Enter, Up, Down, Left, Right, Esc, Tab, Backspace, Delete, F1-F12, PageUp, PageDown, Home, End, Ctrl-a to Ctrl-z). Use it for interactive programs, sudo password prompts you must not see, REPLs and tmux; use exec for ordinary commands. Every complete line (ended by Enter) is classified like an exec command: forbidden lines are refused with `forbidden`, risky lines are always a manual approval, credential files need allowSensitive; a line built with history, completion or cursor keys cannot be inspected and counts as risky. The response carries the `cursor` from before the keystrokes: pass it as session_read's sinceCursor (with waitFor) to read the result. If the user pressed a key in that tab within the last 3 seconds the call fails with `user_typing`; retry later.

allowSensitive.description: Set only after the user agreed that credential files or the environment may be touched.

keys.description: Named keys typed after `text`, in order.

reason.description: Shown to the user in the approval prompt.

requestId.description: Optional shortcut to continue an earlier { status: 'pending' } request (it lives 2 minutes): pass the requestId instead of repeating the arguments. Repeating the identical call also continues it.

target.description: Live session id returned by session_list (or session_open).

text.description: Text to type. Include \r (or a real newline) to press Enter.

tools.title: 向会话输入文本

tools.description: Send a control character to a live session: interrupt (Ctrl-C), eof (Ctrl-D), suspend (Ctrl-Z) or quit (Ctrl-\). Needs approval like exec. Fails with `user_typing` while the user is typing in that tab.

reason.description: Shown to the user in the approval prompt.

target.description: Live session id returned by session_list (or session_open).

tools.title: 向会话发送控制信号

tools.description: Hand a session over to the user: select its tab in NextShell and, at most once per 60 seconds, raise the window. Use it when you need the user to look at or type into the tab (a password, a prompt, a result). Other tools never switch tabs or take the keyboard. Needs approval like exec.

tools.description: Show whether MCP is enabled and halted (emergency stop), whether auto-approve is on and until when, and this client's own pending approval requests (requestId, tool, summary, tier, age). Works while halted.

tools.description: Withdraw one of your own pending approval requests (id from a { status: 'pending' } reply or agent_status) so the user is not asked. Unknown or other clients' ids answer `not_found`.
